summary: The common dandelion is a herbaceous perennial native to Eurasia, now established across several other continents. Its yellow flower heads mature into silver-tufted fruits carried by the wind, while many lineages also produce seeds without fertilisation. This combination of prolific seed production, long-lived buried seed and regeneration from taproot fragments helps it colonise disturbed ground. Its flowers provide early pollen, although that pollen can lack nutrients essential to bees.

details.use: used to flavour wine and to make jam or syrup
details.scope: Wine and soft-drink uses are described for Europe; flower syrup is described in Silesia, other parts of Poland and elsewhere.

details.use: used as a non-caffeinated coffee substitute

summary: Kousa dogwood is a small deciduous tree native to East Asia, including Korea, China and Japan. In spring, conspicuous whitish bracts surround clusters of much smaller yellowish flowers; later, the tree bears round pink-to-red compound fruit with sweet pulp. It is resistant to dogwood anthracnose, a disease to which flowering dogwood is highly susceptible, and this resistance has encouraged its planting in affected areas.

details.use: edible but usually discarded because it is tough and bitter

summary: Betony is a patch-forming herbaceous perennial native to Europe, western Asia and northern Africa. It grows from rhizomes in dry grassland, meadows and open woods, producing upright stems of purple flowers in midsummer. The plant also has a long medicinal history: Pliny praised it highly, medieval and early modern herbals assigned it numerous remedies, and monks and apothecaries commonly cultivated it for medicinal purposes.

Sydney blue gum is a tall tree endemic to eastern Australia, where it grows mainly in sheltered forests near the coast on clay, loam and alluvial sands. After bushfire it can regenerate from buds beneath the bark on its trunk and lower branches, and individual trees live for more than two centuries. Its flowers, leaves and seeds feed flying foxes, koalas and crimson rosellas, while its honey-coloured timber is valued for construction, flooring, furniture and boats.

The European nettle tree is a deciduous tree native to southern Europe, North Africa and Asia Minor. It tolerates drought and nutrient-poor soil but not shade, and often grows in wooded ravines and beside streams. Archaeological finds of its seeds and wood at Iron Age sites support its long presence in the Levant. Its small purple fruits are popular with birds, while its tough, flexible wood has been used by turners and for walking sticks.

Globe amaranth is an edible tropical annual native to Central America, including Panama and Guatemala. Its true flowers are small, but colourful rounded flower heads are conspicuous and retain their colour after drying. Bees, butterflies and other insects pollinate the flowers. That durability also gives the plant cultural roles: it is used for long-lasting leis in Hawaii and for protective festival garlands during Bhai Tika in Nepal.

details.use: source of red-violet betacyanins used as natural food dye

summary: The sacred fir is an evergreen conifer native to high mountain cloud forests in central and southern Mexico and western Guatemala. Cool, humid summers, dry winters and regular snow near the upper edge of its range suit the tree. Its forests provide the preferred winter colony sites for most migrating monarch butterflies in the region. Logging and other disturbance are shrinking its distribution, and experimental plantings at higher elevations are testing a response to projected climate change.

Knautia subscaposa is an herbaceous flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In mainland Portugal it grows in scrub clearings on dry, base-rich soils. A national assessment conducted in 2016–2019 classified it as Endangered and estimated fewer than 250 mature plants in two small, separated subpopulations. Agricultural revival, expansion of eucalyptus plantations and intensive olive groves were identified as threats, while seed banking, nursery propagation and continued monitoring were proposed for conservation.
reviewFlags: The Portuguese population estimate and Endangered assessment date from surveys conducted in 2016–2019 and should not be presented as current without review.

summary: Algerian ivy is a vigorous evergreen climber native to the North African coast and its coastal mountains. Aerial roots let it cling to surfaces, while mature flowering branches bear differently shaped leaves from the juvenile stems. Its coastal origin helps explain a combination of moisture needs and better drought tolerance than many related ivies. In mild lowlands it can naturalise and may become invasive; dense ground cover can also conceal dry material that creates a fire hazard.

summary: The Swedish service-tree is a medium-sized deciduous whitebeam native to Norway, eastern Sweden, south-western Finland and parts of Latvia. It arose through hybridisation among rowan and whitebeam relatives and is tetraploid, carrying four chromosome sets. Like its related polyploid species, it reproduces by apomixis, forming true-to-type seeds without pollination. Its bright red autumn fruit is eaten by thrushes and waxwings, which disperse the seeds.

Blueblossom is an evergreen shrub endemic to Oregon and California, where it can grow more than six metres tall and wide in chaparral. In spring it produces clusters of tiny flowers ranging from blue to nearly white above glossy foliage. Birds, butterflies and other pollinators are drawn to the plant, and honeybees often visit for its pollen. Although it is also called Californian lilac, it is not closely related to true lilacs in the genus Syringa.

Hoary rock-rose is a shrubby plant native to the central and eastern Mediterranean Basin, from parts of Morocco and the western Mediterranean islands east to Turkey and the Levant. It usually bears pink flowers, though the species is notably variable. Its naming has often caused confusion: many authors have called it Cistus incanus, while the true Cistus × incanus is a hybrid between two other rock-rose species.

Coronilla repanda is a flowering plant in the pea family. Both subspecies listed from mainland Portugal, C. repanda subsp. repanda and C. repanda subsp. dura, are described as native there. Neither is listed as protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation in the supplied account.

Andryala arenaria is a flowering plant in the daisy family. Two subspecies, A. arenaria subsp. arenaria and A. arenaria subsp. parvipila, are listed as native to mainland Portugal. The supplied account states that neither is protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.

Musa balbisiana is a wild banana native to eastern South Asia, northern Southeast Asia and southern China. Along with Musa acuminata, it is an ancestor of modern cultivated bananas and contributed their B genome. Its blue-green wild fruit contains conspicuous seeds and is generally considered inedible for that reason, but naturally occurring polyploid clones can produce edible bananas. This link between wild and cultivated forms makes the species important to understanding banana domestication.

reviewFlags: The claimed historical use of wild bananas is explicitly presented as an assumption, and the food evidence distinguishes seeded fruit from naturally seedless clones.

summary: Scrophularia herminii is a flowering plant in the figwort family and is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It occurs in mainland Portugal, where the supplied account states that it is protected under Annex V of the Habitats Directive.

Silene gracilis is a flowering plant in the pink family and is described as native to mainland Portugal. The supplied account states that it is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.

Curio ficoides is a succulent shrub indigenous to South Africa. Its brittle, spreading branches can rise above a metre, losing their lower leaves as they grow. The upright leaves are blue-green to blue-grey, coated with a powdery bloom and flattened from side to side. That knife-like cross-section helps distinguish it from the similar Curio talinoides, whose leaves are rounded and cylindrical.
Dryopteris azorica is a wood fern in the family Dryopteridaceae and is endemic to the Azores archipelago.

The miniature tree fern is a tropical fern native to New Caledonia and introduced in Fiji. It grows one to two metres tall, with bright green fronds rising from a vertical rhizome that resembles a trunk. The species does not tolerate temperatures below 15°C, so in temperate regions it requires year-round protection under glass, along with acidic soil and partial shade.

Lantana horrida is a flowering plant in the verbena family, recorded from Mexico and the West Indies south into subtropical South America. It occupies a broad range of habitats, including tropical savanna, forest, mountains, shrubland and grassland. The species is sometimes confused with Lantana urticoides because several names once treated as forms of L. horrida now belong to that species; unlike L. urticoides, L. horrida has not been documented north of Mexico.

Smooth-stalked sedge is a sedge of moist, shady lowland habitats in western and central Europe, especially alder–ash woodland. Tiny red dots on its utricles help distinguish it from similar sedges such as Carex binervis and Carex distans. James Edward Smith first described the species in 1800.

The false African violet is an evergreen flowering perennial native to Kenya and Tanzania. It belongs to the Streptocarpella subgroup of Streptocarpus and often produces flowers almost throughout the year. A compact cultivated form is recognised as a houseplant by the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit.
Lemanea fluviatilis is an alga in the family Lemaneaceae, native to Europe and North America.
Comb-moss, Ctenidium molluscum, is a moss in the family Hypnaceae. It is native across Eurasia and North America.
